SPLIT. Proven from the producer: meeting-participation-resolver.service.ts emits identity.displayName ?? winning?.subjectName, and subjectName is a guest session's guestName, a booking's bookerName or an invitation's inviteeName (participation-evidence.service.ts). MEMBER delegates to AuraPersonIdentity; the external branch keeps the evidence's own name. Deliberately NOT converged to the canonical LABEL — see governedNonPromotion.

governedNonPromotion.rule: The canonical label is for RENDERING a person. This field is not rendered as a name: pre_join_screen pre-fills the entrant's own name box from it and reads absence as 'we do not know who you are'. Returning 'Someone' here would type that word into a stranger's name field and suppress the question that surface exists to ask.
governedNonPromotion.consequence: identityName stays nullable and reports what the resolver actually resolved. Naming an unresolved person remains the renderer's job. This is a person/presentation boundary, not retained person debt: no alias order, envelope unwrap or fallback is decided here — the parsing itself delegates.

meetingIdentityRefBeforeAfter.defect: fromUserJson hardcoded identityType 'AURA_USER' and, on the very next line, defaulted displayName to 'Guest'. An identifiable Aura person was named by an EXTERNAL PARTICIPANT TYPE they do not hold, because their display identity was incomplete. fromJson did the same to any AURA_USER payload with a blank displayName.

auraUserFallbackCorrection.client: The MeetingIdentityRef AURA_USER branch delegates to AuraPersonIdentity, including its unknown-person semantics. No meetings-specific person fallback was created.
auraUserFallbackCorrection.backend: buildAuraUserBookerIdentity no longer emits 'Guest' as the AURA_USER displayName fallback. This is the producer half of the same defect: no client-side fix can undo a literal 'Guest' already written into an Aura person's displayName on the wire. The projection now carries what it knows — name, else handle, else empty — and the client's canonical authority decides how an unnamed person is addressed. This is the ONLY backend change in this pass, and it sits inside the shared identity authority CH-03 has been operating under for three prior commits.

feedActorDisposition.premiseCorrection: The brief describes both actors as consuming handleOrSlug / avatarOrLogoUrl. Verified against source: those normalized union fields are emitted by feed-projection.service.ts for the POST AUTHOR. Neither of these two actor DTOs is built there — FeedSignalActorDto and FeedReplyAuthorDto both carry plainly named displayName / handle / avatarUrl. The client's avatarOrLogoUrl alias was dead tolerance, never a live contract. Recorded because the disposition below rests on the producer, not on field names.

FeedSignalActor.proof: feed-signal.service.ts builds actors through two separate builders: userActor(r.author, ...) sets type 'USER' from a person's displayName/handle/avatarUrl; institutionActor(r.actorInstitution, ...) sets type 'INSTITUTION' from an institution's name/slug/logoUrl. Both reach the same DTO. The union is the producer's, not the client's invention.
FeedSignalActor.outcome: UNION RETAINED. The person branch delegates to AuraPersonIdentity; the institution branch keeps institutionName / institutionSlug / institutionLogoUrl in its own domain's terms. No code path can now read an institution's slug through a person-shaped accessor, because an institution actor holds no person at all.
FeedSignalActor.fallbackSeparation: label names a person by the canonical order and an institution by its own (name, then /slug) — two orders because there are two identity domains, not because a surface re-decided one of them. _SignalLabel in unified_feed_card.dart previously re-decided this per actor type and now asks the actor.
FeedSignalActor.noNewAbstraction: No new actor abstraction was invented. The existing FeedSignalActor type and FeedAuthorType tag were kept.

FeedReplyAuthor.classification: 2 — A PERSON MODEL THAT WAS ACCEPTING INSTITUTION ALIASES
FeedReplyAuthor.proof: feed-reply.service.ts builds EVERY reply author through one builder, userAuthor(row.author, ...), which reads a person and routes to /u/:handle. An institution never authors a reply; institutional affiliation is expressed through the separate context field. The union aliases the client accepted — 'name', 'avatarOrLogoUrl' — are never emitted on this DTO.
FeedReplyAuthor.outcome: FULLY CONVERGED to AuraPersonIdentity. profileRoute keeps an explicit backend-supplied override and otherwise derives from the canonical person. context and presence remain their own state.
FeedReplyAuthor.note: This is the brief's warning in the other direction: reading union aliases here was a private PERSON interpretation dressed as tolerance.

finalClientPersonDeserializationArchitec: The client has exactly ONE person reader, AuraPersonIdentity.fromJson, and exactly one naming order behind it — own name, then handle, then the shared neutral word. Every typed boundary that carries a person delegates to it and keeps its own domain state beside the person rather than inside it. Polymorphic models stay polymorphic: an actor union keeps a person branch and an institution branch that cannot be read through each other, and a meeting identity keeps a person branch and an external-participant branch whose 'Guest' is a truthful statement of what that participant is. Person identity is never answered by a role, a participant type, a session state or an institution, and no surface re-decides how an unresolved person is addressed.
